exact_statement: For any finite Boolean faces f,q under a fixed interior independent core product law and a distinct selector of bias e down to0, let G=f on selector0,q on selector1, and let d be the mass of high core atoms with |a_S|=2^-k,k>=1, and a_S(b_S-a_S)>0. For upper dyadic rounding, lim Jhi(G)=Jhi(f)-ln4*d. For complete singleton-preserving high references with high mass M, rounded weight Z, mantissa Lhi, n=Mln(Z/M),K=KL(P||Q)=n-Lhi, the limits are Z+3d,Lhi+ln4*d,n+Mln(1+3d/Z), K+Mln(1+3d/Z)-ln4*d, respectively; M=0 is treated by zero charges. Thus Jhi+n-K transports exactly with both full endpoint reference laws. On fair cores, zero-jump input-reflected T2^n completion is equivalent to the dangerous-set parity equations and forbidden-face exclusions. Every essential fair3- or4-bit core admits such an eligible zero-jump completion. For the essential fair5-bit core positive only at00000, every one of32 reflected T2^5 faces is eligible and gives a prime6-bit completion; outward-atom counts by reflection weight r=0..5 are6,5,10,9,6,5, so minimum lost mass is5/256. The best limit is99ln4/256 versus seed104ln4/256; its full limiting KL is [26ln(41/26)-5ln4]/256>0. No reflection in this stated completion class eliminates that jump; no other completion class or universal FEI payment is excluded.
